main_text.l: 1 In medio dictionis post vocalem brevem
nisi sit sub litera daghessata.
2. Post vocalem longam accentu notatam.
3 In fine dictionis etiam geminum.
Apud Chaldæos Scheva simplex quiescit etiam
post vocalem longam quamcunque, ut [illegible, ~6 letters] petitio Dan. 4. 14.
Omnibus literis Scheva convenit, at cum א &
ה rarissime reperitur.
Gutturales nunquam admittunt Scheva vocale,
sed solum mutum, at Scheva compositum est ipso-
rum proprium.
De Dipthongis.
ו & י post Camets, Tsere, Pathach & Chirec in
sine dictionis, cum vocalibus hisce dipthongos
constituunt, ו triplicem facit dipthongum, viz. 1. (au) per ּ,
ut [illegible, ~3 letters] mansuetus, sæpe interveni-
ente ו ut [illegible, ~3 letters] vel per , ut [illegible, ~3 letters] regula. 2. (eu) ut [illegible,
~4 letters] pacificus. 3. (iu) ut [illegible, ~3 letters] os ejus.
ו etiam triplicem facit ai, oi, et ui, ut [illegible,
~3 letters] panai, [illegible, ~2 letters] goi, [illegible, ~3 letters] galui, Judæi vero dipthon-
gum in ו non agnoscunt, sed ו ut consonam pro-
nunciant, & de ו dubitatur à quibusdam. Irregul-
are est [illegible, ~5 letters] Jer 26. 18. quod legendum
& pronunciandum [illegible, ~5 letters] Jerushalajim.
Apud Chaldæos fit (eu) dipthongus ex ו tum in
fine ut apud Hebræos, tum in medio, ut [illegible, ~4
letters] bestia, ubi & ו intervenit.
Jod facit (ai) dipthongum apud Chaldæos, per ו
ante ' in medio ut [illegible, ~4 letters] prima. Dan.7.4.

page.notes: Hebrew and Aramaic words are printed with vowel points; I could not read them letter by letter, so each is marked illegible with an approximate letter count. Mixed-up Hebrew letters in the rules (ו, י, א, ה) are read from the scan but not verified against the points. The Hebrew word for "petitio" and the Hebrew letters near "ut" in the dipthong examples are the least certain. Printed "Jer 26. 18." and "Dan.7.4." are copied as printed. The running head is absent, and the text on this page is a continuous block with no margin notes.
